university: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry

documents.title: Generative AI at ESF
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on academic use and gives no tiers. It says "Generative AI requires human input, editing, and evaluation", recommends entering ESF data only in approved tools, and lists tools offered to "Students, Faculty, and Staff" with learning resources. AI is welcomed as a campus offering but with no requirement, so "encourage" fits best.
documents.summary: A short IT-hosted page that frames generative AI as changing work and study, asks users to review and own AI output, and recommends entering ESF data only in approved tools. It lists provided tools (Copilot, Gemini, Adobe Express, Claude, Mentor.AI) and AI-literacy resources. It has no teaching, integrity, or disclosure policy.

units.why: Opening framing sentence stating that generative AI is "redefining what it means to work, study, teach, and create"; it sets the purpose of the page rather than a rule, so it is an institution-level framing (P56, the nearest fit) and informs only.
units.anchor: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are redefining what it means to work,
units.fit_note: Framing sentence only; it states no principle or scope beyond saying AI changes work and study.

units.why: Defines what generative AI tools do: "generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases". A definition that sets what the page covers, so P61 and informs.
units.anchor: These tools generate new content based on existing data
units.policy: Generative AI tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases, including user or College data in certain applications.

units.why: States that "Generative AI requires human input, editing, and evaluation", a principle that people stay in the loop and are the evaluators; closest to P32 (human remains the thinker). P31 fits less well because it does not say output is wrong.
units.anchor: Generative AI requires human input, editing, and evaluation.
units.fit_note: Stated as a fact about the technology, addressed to all users, not specifically to students.

units.why: "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it our own" tells users to check AI output (P31), and "make it our own" asks them to own the result. I chose P31 because accuracy review is the main point; ownership is secondary.
units.anchor: to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it our own.
units.policy: Users have a responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy and make it their own.

units.why: "It is recommended that users should only enter SUNY ESF data when working in the following approved generative AI tools" is a soft rule (should) steering data entry to vetted tools, which is P50 (protect data, prefer vetted tools).
units.anchor: It is recommended that users should only enter SUNY ESF
units.policy: It is recommended that users should only enter SUNY ESF data when working in the following approved generative AI tools, Microsoft Co-Pilot and Adobe Express Generative AI, which meet security and compliance standards.

units.why: Lists "Microsoft Co-Pilot" as a tool for "Students, Faculty, and Staff", powered by GPT-5. The institution provides it, so it is a sanctioned tool (P17), as an offering and not a mandate.
units.anchor: Tools for Students, Faculty, and Staff
units.frag_start: Tools for Students, Faculty, and Staff
units.frag_end: the same model that powers ChatGPT).
units.policy: Microsoft Co-Pilot is available as a tool for students, faculty, and staff, powered by OpenAI's latest GPT-5 model.

units.why: Says Google Gemini "is also now available" through SU Net ID, with coding assistance; the institution supplies a licensed tool, so P17 with permit.
units.anchor: is also now available, including access to Google's 2.5 Pro Model featuring
units.policy: Google Gemini is available through SU Net ID, including Google's 2.5 Pro Model with guided learning, coding assistance, a canvas editor, and image generation.

units.why: Describes Adobe Express powered by Adobe Firefly as usable "to generate images, videos, social posts, posters"; a provided and approved tool (P17).
units.anchor: can be used to generate images, videos, social posts,
units.policy: Adobe Express, powered by Adobe Firefly, can be used to generate images, videos, social posts, posters, and more from a text prompt.

units.why: Presents Claude (chat, co-work, code) with "Use Claude Chat for every day work", offered as an available tool and recommended for everyday work; a provided tool (P17), unit stance permit.
units.anchor: includes chat, co-work, and code. Use Claude Chat for every day work, Claude Co-Work
units.policy: Claude is available, with Claude Chat for everyday work and Claude Co-Work to work autonomously on knowledge work such as research, analysis, file organization, and producing finished documents, spreadsheets, and decks.

units.why: Describes Claude Code as "an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands on your behalf" and lists it among offered tools. It covers an autonomous coding agent (P07 is about rules for agents), but here the page endorses it and sets no limits, so I chose P17 and note the agent aspect.
units.anchor: coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands on your behalf.
units.frag_start: and Claude Code as an agentic
units.policy: Claude Code is offered as an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, and runs commands on your behalf.
units.fit_note: Also names an autonomous coding agent, but gives no rule on agent use.

units.why: Says Mentor.AI "has pre-created agends to be discovered or you can create your own", another institution-provided tool (P17).
units.anchor: has pre-created agends to be discovered or you can create your own.
units.policy: Mentor.AI offers pre-created agents to discover, and users can create their own.

units.why: Points users to a Moon library guide covering "a history of AI, guidance on how to ask better questions, evaluating AI resources" and AI in academia. Provides AI-literacy resources to the community, so P70.
units.anchor: for a history of AI, guidance on how to ask better questions, evaluating AI resources,
units.frag_start: Check out the Moon library guide
units.policy: Users are directed to the Moon library guide for a history of AI, guidance on how to ask better questions, evaluating AI resources, and information on AI in academia.

units.why: Directs users to the "Google AI Fundamentals course" offered free via a SUNY and Google partnership; an AI-literacy offering (P70).
units.anchor: offered for free as part of a partnership between SUNY and Google.
units.policy: Users are encouraged to take the Google AI Fundamentals course, offered for free as part of a partnership between SUNY and Google.

units.why: Points to the KnowBe4 training library about "AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity"; this is training on AI and security, matching P70 better than P75 since it does not describe phishing or deepfake threats.
units.anchor: Learn about AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity in the SUNY ESF
units.policy: Users are pointed to the SUNY ESF KnowBe4 training library to learn about AI's impact on technology and cybersecurity.

units.why: Offers watching "AI Trends and Opportunities" with CNS and DeepSeas, framing AI as an opportunity; P70 fits as an offered learning resource (P44 is about teaching effective use).
units.policy: Users are invited to watch AI Trends and Opportunities with CNS and DeepSeas.

units.why: Refers users to Syracuse University's ITS Generative AI website for tools and videos; extra institution-provided resources, so P17 as tools from a partner institution.
units.anchor: AI tools and videos provided by Syracuse University can be found on the
units.policy: AI tools and videos provided by Syracuse University can be found on the SU ITS Generative AI website.

units.why: Tells people to "Reach out to the Help Desk" for help; a pointer to human support (P72).
units.anchor: Reach out to the Help Desk
units.frag_start: Reach out to the Help Desk
units.policy: Users who need additional help reach out to the Help Desk.
units.fit_note: Help is about IT help generally, not specifically AI use.

notes: Thin IT page; no academic-integrity or instructional AI policy. Stance encourage is a judgment since it is promotional about provided tools.
